We continued the [action plan](../action-plan.qmd) by inspecting the cancelled comparison
job, reviewing its runner and analysing the already saved Newton trace. The scheduler still
records a root cancellation without a cause. Current node status cannot explain that earlier
event. The owner or scheduler support must resolve it before a fresh submission.

The runner previously returned success for coarse-tolerance solves. Those results could
enter the profile comparison despite falling short of fine convergence. Execution and
comparison now reject them. New output records the host and actual CPU affinity. The batch
script selects allowed CPU IDs and requests a separately timed warm-up step. Execution then
starts again from the initial state. Final accepted-state guard diagnostics run after timing;
they do not count fallback calls within solver iterations.

Focused checks exercise rejection and overlapping trace intervals: [11 performance-tool checks pass in full and Tier-A-only modes]{.claim}[C-147](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-147){.cid .st-tested}.
A bounded local smoke run also checks the host runner's warm-up and final guard output.
It supplies execution evidence, not a reference comparison or speed-up measurement.

The saved Newton trace has [72059 complete HLO events with about 5.369 s of covered trace time]{.claim}[C-148](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-148){.cid .st-preliminary}. Taking the union of event intervals avoids
counting overlap twice, but every recorded operation still belongs to the same fused module
and runtime source. That does not identify ensemble inference, geometry or Jacobian cost.
The performance ceiling remains open.

A concrete bounded comparison request is ready for review after the scheduler issue is
resolved. No new cluster job has been submitted. RF and pedestal reference selection remains
the other prerequisite for completing M3.
